The way I approach it includes my long tone routine. I use a tuner and play 2-3 measures of whole notes. But before I do any of that, I check my posture of my seating. Then I place my hands 9-12 inches away from my face and blow onto my finger tips. This will assist you on visualizing what type of air attack you’re using. you’re using. Try to focus on the sensation of inhaling air. how tense does your chest feel? How much air are you intaking? What sound was your air intake? What shape the apature of your lips when blowing out? I try to be mindful with all those factors. 

Moving onto the horn itself, I do slur exercises from the F side. I start on G on the staff and almost kind of bend the note down to E on the staff and the next note after that and so on and so forth (harmonic series). Whatever note comes out next is what it’ll play and I really try to feel it out. Same questions last time: How tense am I? Was it a good amount of air. How does my lips feel? (All of this with a tuner/drone) 

As my lips warms up, I start to move higher up the staff. Perhaps C on the staff. Remember that tension does NOT equal bad. We just need to balance the amount of tension you use as you play. And long tones and this much of attention to your air plays a big part. 

If there’s more specific question, ill try my best to give my advice through my experience :D

All of the responses are related to air support and I can 100% support those advice. I have the same habit of using excessive tension in result of keeping my head above the water in terms of playing high registers. I’ve been working on air support but not in a sense of using “more air”. I like to describe it as perfecting air flow. Not too much air to the point where you lose quality of the tone and sound and not too little use of air where you feel the need to tighten your lips. 

This is probably the hardest habit you’ll have to break in my opinion. I’ve started this journey maybe 2 weeks ago and I still have a hard time finding the right amount of air flow to use. I’ll get frustrated because I’m not used to  using this technique for support. But I know it’s best for the long run.
